title: Customers were charged twice
intro: Finance reports 214 customers charged twice last night between 02:10 and 02:25. During that window the payment workers were restarted by a deploy. The payments flow is: checkout publishes a 'charge' message to a queue, and a worker calls the payment provider and then acknowledges the message.

steps.prompt: Find a duplicated charge in the database: list order ids with more than one row in the charges table.
expected_commands: psql -c "SELECT order_id, count(*) FROM charges GROUP BY order_id HAVING count(*) > 1 LIMIT 5;"
psql -c "SELECT order_id, count(*) FROM charges GROUP BY order_id HAVING count(*) > 1 LIMIT 5"

steps.prompt: Look at both charges for order 881204.
expected_commands: psql -c "SELECT id, order_id, amount, provider_ref, created_at FROM charges WHERE order_id = 881204;"

steps.prompt: Two real charges, 35 seconds apart, with different provider references. See what the worker logged for that order around 02:11.
steps.fake_output:
02:11:03 worker-7c9d charging order 881204
02:11:04 worker-7c9d provider charge ok ch_3Pq1a7 for order 881204
02:11:04 worker-7c9d received SIGTERM, shutting down
02:11:38 worker-5b8e charging order 881204 (redelivered)
02:11:39 worker-5b8e provider charge ok ch_3Pq1c2 for order 881204
steps.hint: Grep the workers' logs for the order id.

steps.prompt: The first worker charged the card, then was killed before acknowledging the message, so the queue delivered it again. Check whether the worker sends an idempotency key to the provider: search its source for 'Idempotency-Key'.
No idempotency key anywhere. Add a database guard so a second charge for the same order can never be stored: create a unique index on charges(order_id), named uniq_charges_order.
expected_commands: psql -c "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY uniq_charges_order ON charges (order_id);"
psql -c "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY uniq_charges_order ON charges (order_id)"
psql -c "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uniq_charges_order ON charges (order_id);"
steps.fake_output:
ERROR:  could not create unique index "uniq_charges_order"
DETAIL:  Key (order_id)=(881204) is duplicated.
(the 214 duplicates must be refunded and removed first; then the index can be created)

resolution: The queue did what it promises: at-least-once delivery. The worker took the message, charged the card, and was terminated by the deploy before it could acknowledge. The queue, seeing no acknowledgement, redelivered, and a second worker charged again. No component was faulty; the design assumed each message would be processed exactly once, which no queue can guarantee across an external call. The fix is idempotency at every layer that has a side effect. Send the provider an idempotency key derived from the order (so a repeat request returns the original charge instead of creating a new one), and enforce uniqueness in your own database, so a duplicate can't be recorded even if a bug slips through. Note the last step failed on purpose: you can't add the constraint until the bad data is cleaned up, and those 214 customers need refunds first. Also give workers a graceful shutdown (finish the current message and acknowledge it before exiting) and a long enough termination grace period.
